questions.q: How are companies in Asia using generative AI?
questions.a: Asian companies are using generative AI well beyond chatbots and text. Game studios in Japan and South Korea use it to create environments, character dialogue and textures, while research groups use it to simulate drug compounds. Media and animation studios use it for background art, dubbing scripts and 3D renders.

questions.q: How is generative AI changing game development in Japan and South Korea?
questions.a: Generative AI helps studios produce game assets much faster and with more variety. Square Enix has publicly committed to pushing generative AI into its workflows, and Korean companies like NCSoft and Nexon use it to shorten development cycles. The technology also gives designers more room to experiment with characters and storylines.

questions.q: Why is generative AI growing so quickly in Asia?
questions.a: Several factors work together: plenty of localized data, mobile-first consumers who want personalized content, and government support for research and cloud infrastructure. Lean startup teams across the region are also building specialized models for local industries. That mix makes Asia fertile ground for practical generative AI.

questions.q: What are the biggest challenges for generative AI in Asia?
questions.a: Language diversity is a major hurdle, because training models across many languages takes huge multilingual datasets. Rules on content, privacy and ethics are still evolving and differ by country. Many Southeast Asian startups also struggle to get affordable access to high-performance GPUs and cloud services.

questions.q: How can a business in Asia get started with generative AI?
questions.a: A good first step is to audit your current workflows and find tasks where generative AI could help. From there, you can train your teams to work alongside AI tools and look at partnerships with regional startups that build industry-specific models. It's also wise to keep track of local regulations as they change.
